newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ foreign debt rose NZ$3.6 bln in June qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ foreign debt rose NZ$3.6 bln in June qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's total overseas debt rose NZ$3.6 billion, or 5.1 percent to NZ$74.7 billion between March 31, 1996 and June 30, 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday.
Net new borrowings of NZ$3.97 billion, offset slightly by exchange rate gains of $0.34 billion, drove the quarterly rise in total overseas debt.

Official sector overseas debt rose $1.5 billion in the quarter to $23.4 billion. Official sector overseas debt denominated in New Zealand dollars rose $2.2 billion, offset partly by a $0.7 billion fall in foreign currency debt.
"The rise in New Zealand dollar denominated overseas debt was caused by increased foreign investment in domestically issued securities," SNZ said.

Corporate sector overseas debt, previously called "other sector" by SNZ, rose $2.1 billion in the quarter to $51.3 billion. SNZ said the rise was influenced by increased deposits in NZ financial institutions by overseas residents.
NZ dollar-denominated total overseas debt rose $3.3 billion in the quarter to $39.4 billion, and is $7.5 billion higher than a year ago.
New Zealand's foreign currency debt remained steady at $32.8 billion, down $2.7 billion on a year ago.

Overseas debt held as deposits and domestically issued securities rose sharply during the June quarter, increasing $2.9 billion and $2.0 billion respectively. SNZ said overseas debt had generally been rising over the past two years, driven mainly by domestically issued securities and deposits.
The ratio of total overseas debt to GDP was 84.7 percent, compared with 81.2 percent at March 31, 1996, and 81.1 percent at June 30, 1995.
The ratio of total overseas debt to exports of goods and services for the year to June was 273.9 percent, compared with 263.6 percent at March 31 and 258.3 percent a year ago.
